transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

A door that crashes down when opened usually means the mechanism that holds it in place has lost its tension. In most dishwashers, including Hotpoints, this is caused by worn or broken balance springs (or cables) inside the hinge assembly. It’s a common wear item and not typically an electrical fault. 1. 2. Could you tell me if the door feels physically heavy to lift when you open it, and whether the springs at the hinge look intact? Also, is there a separate kitchen cabinet door covering the dishwasher?

It doesn't feel heavy exactly, one side has a bit of spring in it but the other just feels loose. I can see a loose spring hanging down on the right side with a torch under the plinth. No separate cabinet door, it's got a decor panel on the front.

That suggests it. Dishwasher doors use a pair of springs (or cables) to counterbalance the weight of the heavy door so it stays where you put it. When one breaks or comes off, that side loses all tension and the door falls open. This is a mechanical wear issue rather than an electrical fault. The next step is to source the correct replacement balance springs for your specific Hotpoint model. You can usually find these by searching for "Hotpoint dishwasher door balance springs" along with your model number (found on the rating plate inside the door frame or on the side of the tub). When replacing them, it is best practice to replace both sides even if one looks okay, as they wear at similar rates. Ensure the appliance is isolated from the mains before starting any work near the hinges.
